ui_bugs.issue: `hoursBetween` is called inside shift-start/shift-end onChangeText callbacks (lines 400, 416) but the function is not imported or defined anywhere in the file. Typing into any shift time input will throw ReferenceError and red-screen the editor. Fix: `import { hoursBetween } from '@/src/pricing'` (or wherever it lives) or inline it: `const hoursBetween = (a: string, b: string) => { const p = (s:string)=>{const [h,m]=s.split(':').map(Number); return h*60+(m||0);}; if(!a||!b) return 0; let d = p(b)-p(a); if (d<0) d+=24*60; return Math.round((d/60)*10)/10; }`. Add before component or as util.

`venue` and `setVenue` are referenced in saveAsTemplate (line 175: `venue: venue`) and applyTemplate (line 187: `setVenue(tpl.venue || '')`) but the venue useState was removed when the 'Miejsce' input was deleted. Tapping save-as-template-btn or tpl-apply-{id} will throw ReferenceError. Fix: either re-add `const [venue, setVenue] = useState('')` (still round-tripped by backend) OR replace with hard-coded 'Biesiada pod lasem' (matches line 112) and drop setVenue call.

Cards do not visibly show `created_by_name` chip for existing events (all pre-existing events have empty created_by_name — this is expected). PLEASE VERIFY manually by creating a new event after fix lands: it should show the creator chip. Testing agent could not confirm chip render because there is no test event with created_by_name yet on the seeded account.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py: workspace helpers correct — `ws(user)` returns workspace_id or falls back to user.id; `current_user` also back-fills workspace_id when missing (handles old users). All CRUD (events/staff/templates/expenses/backup) now correctly uses ws(user) for read+write and stamps created_by_id/created_by_name on create — verified in tests.

server.py workspace_join: correctly rejects own code (400), unknown code (404), and updates only current user's workspace_id — good. However, if user A is currently sharing user X's workspace and user B joins A's *invite_code* (=A.id), B ends up on A.id workspace, NOT X's. This is by design (invite_code is your own user.id, not your current workspace_id). Might be worth documenting.

server.py workspace_leave: resets caller's workspace_id to their own id. Note: any items the leaver created while inside the shared workspace remain on the shared workspace (their owner_id was ws(user)=A.id at creation). So a leaver loses access to their OWN previously-created items until they rejoin. This is spec-correct but worth flagging in UX copy.
event/[id].tsx line 94-97: pricing binding is now correct. But `hoursBetween` (lines 400,416) and `venue`/`setVenue` (lines 175,187) are undefined identifiers. `grep` confirms zero definitions.

server.py delete_account still uses `owner_id: uid` (user's personal id) — so if the user was in a shared workspace, their delete_account only removes items they OWN personally, not shared items owned by workspace_id. The current implementation uses `uid` not `ws(user)` intentionally — which is correct so leaver doesn't nuke coworker data. Good.
